scannerInput.title: Reading Input With Scanner
whereToLook: Check that you create a Scanner tied to System.in near the top of main.
Check that the distance is read as an int and stored in a variable before it is used.
Check that the menu choice is read with the same Scanner each time through the loop.

loopsAndMethods.title: The Menu Loop and Conversion Methods
whereToLook: Check that a while loop keeps showing the menu until the user enters 4.
Check that calcKilometers, calcInches, and calcFeet each accept the distance and return a double.
Check that the menu method only displays the four options and takes no arguments.
Check that selecting an option calls the matching calc method rather than repeating the formula inline.

outputFormatting.title: Matching the Required Output
whereToLook: Compare your printed text character-for-character against the Requirements checklist in the README.
Check that you print the value stored in your distance variable, not a typed-in number.
Check that the invalid-selection message is shown before the menu loops back for another choice.

sourceChecks.name: Uses Scanner for input
sourceChecks.message: This challenge requires reading the distance and menu choice with a Scanner. See the 'Reading Input With Scanner' help topic.

sourceChecks.name: Uses a while loop for the menu
sourceChecks.message: The menu should keep repeating using a while loop until the user quits. See the 'Menu Loop and Conversion Methods' help topic.

sourceChecks.name: Defines and calls a menu method
sourceChecks.message: You need a method named menu that displays the four options, and it needs to be called from your loop. See the 'Menu Loop and Conversion Methods' help topic.

sourceChecks.name: Defines the three conversion methods
sourceChecks.message: You need calcKilometers, calcInches, and calcFeet methods, each returning a double. See the 'Menu Loop and Conversion Methods' help topic.

sourceChecks.name: Ends the program when the user quits
sourceChecks.message: When the user selects 4, the program should end (for example, with System.exit) after printing the goodbye message.

tests.name: Prompts for the distance in meters
tests.message: Your program should ask the user to enter a distance in meters using the exact prompt from the README before doing anything else.

tests.name: Displays the full conversion menu
tests.expectedOutput:
1. Convert to kilometers
2. Convert to inches
3. Convert to feet
4. Quit the program
tests.message: Your menu method should display all four options in order, each on its own line, exactly as shown in the README.

tests.name: Converts 500 meters to kilometers
tests.message: When the user selects option 1, use calcKilometers to convert the entered distance and display the result in the required format.

tests.name: Converts 500 meters to inches
tests.message: When the user selects option 2, use calcInches to convert the entered distance and display the result in the required format.

tests.name: Converts 500 meters to feet
tests.message: When the user selects option 3, use calcFeet to convert the entered distance and display the result in the required format.

tests.name: Kilometer conversion uses the entered value
tests.message: Your program should recalculate the kilometer conversion based on whatever distance the user enters, not just the example value.

possibleErrors.message: Your output still shows the answer for 500 meters even though 250 was entered. Make sure calcKilometers is using the value read from the Scanner.

tests.name: Feet conversion uses the entered value
tests.message: Your program should recalculate the feet conversion based on whatever distance the user enters, not just the example value.

possibleErrors.message: Your output still shows the answer for 500 meters even though 1000 was entered. Make sure calcFeet is using the value read from the Scanner.

tests.name: Rejects an invalid menu selection
tests.message: When the user enters a choice that isn't 1-4, display the exact invalid-selection message and let the user try again.

tests.name: Loop allows multiple conversions before quitting
tests.expectedOutput: Thank you. Have a nice day!
tests.message: Your loop should keep showing the menu after each conversion so the user can make several selections before finally quitting with option 4.
